content: {"decision":"Block use until execution is isolated and independently constrained.","risks":["Model-generated shell commands can execute arbitrary code, destroy checkout data, or establish persistence.","Inherited environment and network access enable credential theft, data exfiltration, and unauthorized remote actions.","A model reviewer can miss attacks or be manipulated; its approval is not a security boundary.","Harmless-command tests provide no evidence of containment against malicious commands."],"required_changes":["Treat model output as untrusted. Prefer narrowly scoped structured operations with validated arguments over arbitrary shell execution.","Enforce policy outside both models; deny unsupported operations and require explicit human approval for privileged or external effects.","Execute in an ephemeral sandbox with an unprivileged identity, read-only source input, disposable writable storage, and no host credentials, sockets, or writable checkout mounts.","Use a minimal environment and deny network access by default; narrowly authorize any required destinations and credentials.","Limit runtime, processes, memory, storage, and output; record execution and review changes before applying them to the checkout."],"evidence_needed":["Threat model and independently reviewed sandbox, environment, filesystem, and network policies.","Adversarial tests covering destructive commands, secret access, exfiltration, shell injection, obfuscation, reviewer manipulation, sandbox escape attempts, and resource exhaustion.","Observed enforcement showing forbidden operations fail even when the model reviewer approves them, with host files and credentials protected.","Tests of approval enforcement, fail-closed behavior, cleanup, audit records, and controlled application of resulting changes."]}
